opening_message:
Ticket 1: Miguel Benson (employee ID E006) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E006.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Miguel Benson (E006) is a full-time Engineer and requests admin access to Source Code. Since Engineers own the Source Code system, admin is permitted for full-time employees under policy. Recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E006 (Miguel Benson) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Under policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. Requested admin exceeds the maximum; recommend granting read.
reason: HR note (authoritative for employment type) states E006 Miguel Benson is a full-time Engineer, looked up in the HR database. Engineers own the Source Code system, and the policy permits admin for full-time employees whose role owns the system. The requested level (admin) equals the maximum permitted, so grant admin. Note: the Security note claims contractor status from the security database, but employment type is an HR fact; per the HR record the employee is full-time, so admin is permitted.
